title: The isolated rev-5 source reader (no system Git config) can judge a clean Windows checkout dirty when the checkout used system core.autocrlf=true and the repository has no full .gitattributes eol policy
outcome: On Windows, a worktree checked out under the machine's line-ending configuration is measured clean at its commit by the source reader whenever its content is unchanged, regardless of whether the reader isolates system/global Git config; any remaining mismatch is reported as a named line-ending cause rather than a generic dirty tree.
acceptance: On Windows with system core.autocrlf=true and a repository without a complete eol policy, an unchanged worktree checked out under that system config (including files whose stat cache is stale or racy) is measured clean at its commit by the committed-input reader, and a genuinely changed file is still not clean.

If the reader cannot reconcile the checkout's line-ending conversion with its isolated config, it refuses with a named line-ending cause, not a generic not-clean result; the chosen behaviour is applied identically in Engram's `engram source` command and documented.
Tests cover: autocrlf=true checkout clean (fresh and stale-stat), a real content change, and a repository with a full .gitattributes eol policy (unchanged behaviour).
